t: The Workmen's Compensation Act 1923 was renamed the Employees' Compensation Act by an amendment in:
e: The Workmen's Compensation (Amendment) Act 2009, effective 18 January 2010, renamed the Act as the Employees' Compensation Act 1923 and made it gender-neutral; employers' liability under it is insurable.

t: Under the IRDAI EoM Regulations 2023, the overall expenses of management limit for a stand-alone health insurer is:
e: The 2023 EoM Regulations set the overall limit at 35% of gross written premium for stand-alone health insurers, compared to 30% for general insurers.

topic: IRDAI Health Insurance Regulations - Multiple Policies
t: Priya holds two indemnity-based health policies with different insurers. On hospitalisation, under IRDAI health insurance norms she:
o: Must claim from the insurer whose policy was issued first
Has the right to choose the insurer from whom to claim, and the balance may be claimed from the other insurer
Must claim equally from both insurers
Can claim from only one insurer and forfeits the other
e: IRDAI health regulations and the 2024 master circular give the policyholder the right to choose the policy under which to claim; the other insurer settles the balance subject to its policy terms.

t: An Insurance Marketing Firm (IMF) registered under the IRDAI (Registration of Insurance Marketing Firm) Regulations 2015 is required to have a minimum net worth of:
e: The IMF Regulations 2015 prescribe a minimum net worth of Rs 10 lakh (Rs 5 lakh for IMFs operating in aspirational districts under the 2019 amendment); IMFs operate in a specified area and may distribute other financial products as well.

t: Under Section 42 of the Insurance Act 1938, which of the following is a disqualification for appointment as an insurance agent?
o: Having been found guilty of criminal misappropriation, breach of trust, cheating, forgery or abetment of such offence
Being employed in the private sector
e: Section 42(3) lists disqualifications including minority, unsoundness of mind, conviction for fraud-related offences, and violation of the code of conduct; a graduate degree, age or private employment are not disqualifications.

t: The Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021 increased the foreign direct investment limit in Indian insurance companies to:
e: The Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021 amended Section 2(7A) to permit foreign investment up to 74% in Indian insurance companies; 100% FDI has been proposed but is not the legal position as of 2024.

topic: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024 - Claims
t: Under the 2024 PPHI Regulations for general insurance claims, the surveyor must submit the survey report within how many days of allocation, and the insurer must decide on the claim within how many days of receiving the report?
e: The 2024 PPHI Regulations tightened general insurance claim timelines: survey report within 15 days of allocation (extendable in exceptional cases) and claim decision within 7 days of the final survey report.

t: Under Section 6 of the Insurance Act 1938, the minimum paid-up equity capital for a company carrying on exclusively reinsurance business is:
e: Section 6(1)(b) requires a minimum paid-up equity capital of Rs 200 crore for an insurer carrying on exclusively the business of reinsurance.

topic: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024
t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for life and health policies with a term of one year or more is:
o: 15 days from receipt of policy document
15 days, or 30 days for electronically sourced policies
45 days from receipt of policy document
30 days from the date of receipt of the policy document, irrespective of mode of sale
e: The 2024 PPHI Regulations extended the free-look period to 30 days from receipt of the policy document for all life and health policies of one year or more, replacing the earlier 15/30-day split (position as of 2024).

t: Under the Outsourcing Regulations 2017, insurers must report their outsourcing arrangements to IRDAI:
o: Annually, within 45 days of the close of the financial year, in the prescribed format
Only when the vendor is located outside India
Only if the contract value exceeds Rs 10 crore
e: Regulation 10 requires insurers to file an annual return of all outsourcing arrangements with IRDAI within 45 days of the end of the financial year, along with board-approved outsourcing policy compliance.

t: The minimum educational qualification and training prescribed for a Point of Sales Person (POSP) is:
o: Class 10 pass and 15 hours of in-house training by the insurer or intermediary
Class 10 pass and 25 hours of training by an accredited institute
e: IRDAI's POSP guidelines require a minimum qualification of Class 10, age 18 or above, and 15 hours of training with an in-house examination conducted by the insurer or intermediary that sponsors the POSP.

t: Under the IRDAI (Expenses of Management, including Commission, of Insurers) Regulations 2023 (consolidated in 2024), the overall limit on expenses of management for a general insurer is:
e: The 2023 EoM Regulations prescribe an overall EoM limit of 30% of gross written premium for general insurers, with commission limits removed in favour of a board-approved policy within the EoM cap (position as of 2024).

t: Under the IRDAI (Re-insurance) Regulations 2018, after exhausting the obligatory cession, an Indian insurer must offer the best terms for reinsurance cessions in the following order of preference:
o: Indian reinsurer(s) first, then Foreign Reinsurance Branches (FRBs) and IFSC Insurance Offices (IIOs), then other Indian insurers and cross-border reinsurers
Cross-border reinsurers first, then FRBs, then Indian reinsurer
Any reinsurer offering the lowest price
Lloyd's India first, followed by GIC Re
e: Regulation 5A of the Reinsurance Regulations 2018 (as amended) prescribes order of preference: Indian reinsurers (GIC Re), then FRBs/IIOs with minimum credit rating, then other Indian insurers and cross-border reinsurers.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 read with the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of District, State and National Commissions) Rules 2021, a District Commission can entertain complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed:
e: The 2021 Rules revised pecuniary jurisdiction: District Commission up to Rs 50 lakh, State Commission above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore, and National Commission above Rs 2 crore (position as of 2024).

t: A 68-year-old applies for a fresh individual health insurance policy in 2024. Under current IRDAI norms, the insurer:
o: Must reject the proposal because the maximum entry age is 65
May reject only because age exceeds 60
Cannot refuse solely on grounds of age, since IRDAI removed the 65-year entry age cap in 2024, though it may underwrite and price the risk
Must issue the policy without any underwriting
e: IRDAI's 2024 notification removed the upper age limit of 65 years for purchasing health insurance; insurers must offer products for all age groups, subject to their board-approved underwriting policy (position as of 2024).

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Web Aggregators) Regulations 2017, the minimum paid-up capital required to register as a web aggregator is:
e: Regulation 8 of the Web Aggregators Regulations 2017 requires a minimum paid-up capital of Rs 25 lakh and a net worth of at least Rs 25 lakh to be maintained at all times.

topic: Insurance Institute of India and IIB
t: The Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB), which acts as a central data repository for the Indian insurance industry, was promoted by IRDAI in:
e: IIB was set up by IRDAI in 2009 (registered as a society in 2012) to collect, analyse and disseminate industry data; the Insurance Institute of India, by contrast, dates from 1955 as the Federation of Insurance Institutes.

t: Under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, the provision making third-party insurance compulsory for every motor vehicle used in a public place is:
e: Section 146 of the MV Act 1988 (Chapter XI) requires every motor vehicle used in a public place to be covered by a policy of insurance against third-party liability complying with Section 147.

t: Which of the following can be appointed as a micro-insurance agent under the Micro Insurance Regulations 2015?
o: Only individual agents who have passed IC-38
NGOs, Self-Help Groups, Micro-Finance Institutions, RBI-regulated NBFC-MFIs, District Cooperative Banks, Business Correspondents and similar entities
e: Regulation 2 of the Micro Insurance Regulations 2015 lists NGOs, SHGs, MFIs, RRBs, DCCBs, PACS, business correspondents and others as eligible micro-insurance agents.

t: Regulations made by IRDAI under Section 26 of the IRDA Act 1999 must be:
o: Laid before each House of Parliament
Ratified by the Life and General Insurance Councils
Published only on the IRDAI website
e: Section 27 of the IRDA Act requires every rule and regulation made by the Government or the Authority to be laid before each House of Parliament, which may modify or annul them.

t: After the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015, an appeal against an order passed by IRDAI lies with the:
e: Section 110 of the Insurance Act, as amended in 2015, provides that any person aggrieved by an order of IRDAI may appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal within 45 days.

t: Within three years of issuance, when an insurer repudiates a life policy on the ground of fraud under Section 45, it must:
o: Communicate in writing to the insured or legal representatives/nominees/assignees the grounds and materials on which the decision is based
Obtain prior approval of the Insurance Ombudsman
Refund all premiums with interest at bank rate plus 2%
File a report with the Life Insurance Council
e: Section 45(2) requires the insurer to communicate in writing the grounds and materials on which the repudiation for fraud is based to the insured, legal representatives, nominees or assignees.

t: Under IRDAI's rural and social sector obligation regulations, the 'social sector' includes:
o: Only persons below the poverty line
Only residents of villages with a population below 5,000
Unorganised sector, informal sector, economically vulnerable or backward classes and other categories of persons, including persons with disability
e: The IRDAI (Obligations of Insurers to Rural and Social Sectors) Regulations define social sector to include the unorganised and informal sectors, economically vulnerable or backward classes, and persons with disabilities, in both rural and urban areas.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015), no life insurance policy can be called in question on any ground whatsoever after the expiry of:
o: Two years from the date of issuance of the policy
Three years from the date of the proposal
Five years from the date of commencement of risk
Three years from the date of issuance, commencement of risk, revival or addition of rider, whichever is later
e: Section 45(1) bars any challenge to a life policy after three years from the latest of the date of issuance, commencement of risk, revival, or rider addition.

t: Section 40 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits an insurer from paying commission or remuneration for soliciting or procuring insurance business to:
o: Any person other than an insurance agent or intermediary duly appointed or registered under the Act
Any corporate agent that is also a bank
Any broker whose remuneration exceeds 15% of premium
e: Section 40(1) bars payment of commission or remuneration in any form to anyone other than a duly appointed insurance agent or a registered intermediary.

t: Under the IRDAI (Third Party Administrators - Health Services) Regulations 2016, the minimum paid-up equity share capital for a TPA is:
e: Regulation 6 of the TPA Regulations 2016 requires a minimum paid-up equity capital of Rs 4 crore, with working capital of not less than Rs 1 crore at all times.

t: Ramesh assigned his life policy to his bank as security for a housing loan. What happens to the existing nomination in favour of his wife under Section 39?
o: The nomination is cancelled and must be freshly made after the loan is repaid
The nomination becomes invalid until the bank issues a no-objection certificate
The nomination is not cancelled; it is only affected to the extent of the insurer's or assignee's interest in the policy
e: Section 39(4) provides that an assignment to the insurer or to a lender as security for a loan does not cancel the nomination but only affects the nominee's rights to the extent of the lender's interest.

t: Under the 2024 Health Insurance master circular, after how many months of continuous coverage (moratorium period) can a health insurer no longer contest a claim on grounds of non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for established fraud?
e: The moratorium period was reduced from 8 years (96 months) to 60 months of continuous coverage, after which no policy can be contested except for proven fraud or permanent exclusions.

t: Under Section 4 of the IRDA Act 1999, the Authority consists of a Chairperson and:
o: Not more than three whole-time members and two part-time members
Not more than five whole-time members and not more than four part-time members
Not more than seven whole-time members and three part-time members
e: Section 4 of the IRDA Act 1999 provides for a Chairperson, not more than five whole-time members and not more than four part-time members, all appointed by the Central Government.

t: Which requirement for Indian insurance companies was removed by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021 and the consequent Indian Insurance Companies (Foreign Investment) Amendment Rules 2021?
o: The requirement that the company be 'Indian owned and controlled'
The requirement of a minimum paid-up capital of Rs 100 crore
The requirement to obtain a certificate of registration
The requirement to maintain a solvency margin
e: Along with raising FDI to 74%, the 2021 amendment deleted the 'Indian owned and controlled' condition from Section 2(7A), replacing it with safeguards on board composition and resident Indian KMPs.

t: The fundamental difference between an insurance broker and an insurance agent is that a broker:
o: Represents the client (prospective insured) and not the insurer
Can sell only life insurance products
Cannot receive remuneration from the insurer
e: Under the Brokers Regulations 2018, a broker acts for and represents the insured/client in arranging insurance, whereas an agent is appointed by and represents the insurer; brokers are nonetheless remunerated by insurers.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was formally established as a statutory body on:
e: Although the IRDA Act was passed in December 1999, the Authority was constituted as a statutory body with effect from 19 April 2000; it was renamed IRDAI by the 2015 amendment.

t: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act 2002, insurers are classified as 'reporting entities' and are required to furnish prescribed reports to:
e: Section 12 of PMLA read with the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules 2005 requires reporting entities, including insurers, to furnish cash and suspicious transaction reports to the Director, FIU-IND.

t: A complainant approached the insurer with a grievance and received a rejection letter on 1 February 2024. Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, the complaint to the Ombudsman must be filed within:
o: One year from the date of rejection by the insurer
Two years from the date of rejection
Three years from the date of loss
Six months from the date of policy issue
e: Rule 14(3) requires the complaint to be made within one year after the insurer rejects the representation or after the expiry of one month if the insurer fails to reply.

t: The body that administers the Insurance Ombudsman scheme and appoints Ombudsmen under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017 (as amended in 2021) is the:
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
e: The 2021 amendment renamed the Executive Council of Insurers as the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen, which administers the scheme; Ombudsmen are selected through a committee chaired by the IRDAI Chairperson.

topic: Insurance Act 1938 - Sec 64VB Premium in Advance
t: Sunita paid her motor policy premium by cheque on 1 April and the policy was issued the same day. The cheque was dishonoured on 5 April. Her car was damaged in an accident on 3 April. What is the legal position under Section 64VB?
o: No risk was assumed since the premium was never realised; the insurer is not liable
The insurer is liable because the loss occurred before the dishonour
The insurer is liable but may recover the premium from the claim amount
The insurer is liable only for third-party liability
e: Under Section 64VB, where a cheque is dishonoured the premium is deemed never to have been received and no risk attaches; the insurer must inform the insured and treat the policy as void ab initio.

topic: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024 - Proposals
t: Under the IRDAI PPHI Regulations 2024, an insurer must process a proposal and communicate its decision to the proposer within:
o: 15 days of receipt of the proposal
7 days of receipt of the proposal
30 days of receipt of the proposal
45 days of receipt of the proposal
e: The 2024 PPHI Regulations shortened the proposal processing timeline to 7 days from the earlier 15 days (position as of 2024).

t: Under Section 38 of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015), an insurer may decline to act upon an assignment of a life policy when:
o: It has sufficient reason to believe the assignment is not bona fide, not in the interest of the policyholder, or is for the purpose of trading in the policy, and it records the reasons in writing
The assignee is a relative of the policyholder
The policy has run for less than three years
The assignment is made to a bank as security for a loan
e: Section 38(2) permits an insurer to decline to act upon an endorsement or deed of assignment on these grounds, with reasons recorded in writing and communicated to the policyholder within 30 days.

t: Under Section 105C of the Insurance Act 1938 (inserted in 2015), the maximum penalty for failure to comply with rural and social sector obligations under Sections 32B and 32C is:
e: Section 105C provides for a penalty of up to Rs 25 crore, and in case of continued default, cancellation of registration, for failure to meet rural, social or third-party motor obligations.

t: A general insurer reports a solvency ratio of 1.40 at the end of a quarter. Under IRDAI norms, the likely consequence is:
o: No action, since the ratio exceeds 100%
Mandatory merger with a public sector insurer
Breach of the 150% control level, triggering IRDAI directions such as a capital infusion/financial plan and restrictions on business
e: Section 64VA(2) read with IRDAI regulations treats a ratio below the 150% control level as a breach, requiring the insurer to submit a financial plan to restore solvency and enabling IRDAI to impose restrictions.

t: Section 64VA of the Insurance Act 1938 deals with:
o: Sufficiency of assets, i.e. maintenance of the required solvency margin by insurers
e: Section 64VA requires every insurer to maintain at all times an excess of value of assets over liabilities of not less than the required solvency margin as specified by IRDAI regulations.

topic: IRDAI Appointment of Insurance Agents Regulations
t: Under the 2016 Agents Regulations, the appointment letter to an insurance agent is issued by:
o: The Life or General Insurance Council
The insurer, through its designated official
e: Since 2015, agent licensing by IRDAI was replaced by appointment by the insurer; the designated official of the insurer issues the appointment letter after verifying the Central Agency Database.

t: Under the PML Rules, a Cash Transaction Report (CTR) must be filed by an insurer for all cash transactions of value exceeding Rs 10 lakh (or integrally connected transactions aggregating to that amount) by the:
o: Last day of the same month
e: Rule 8 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules 2005 requires CTRs to be furnished to FIU-IND every month by the 15th day of the succeeding month.

topic: IRDAI Appointment of Insurance Agents Regulations
t: The pre-recruitment qualifying examination for individual insurance agents in India is based on course material IC-38 and is conducted by:
e: Under the IRDAI (Appointment of Insurance Agents) Regulations 2016, the agency examination (IC-38) is conducted by the Insurance Institute of India or an examination body approved by IRDAI.

t: Under the PMLA 2002 and PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, reporting entities such as insurers must maintain records of transactions and client identity for a period of:
o: 3 years from the date of transaction
10 years from the date of transaction
1 year from the end of the business relationship
5 years from the date of transaction or, for identity records, 5 years after the business relationship ends
e: Section 12 of PMLA, as amended in 2012, requires maintenance of transaction records for five years from the transaction date and identity records for five years after the end of the business relationship.

t: Under the IRDAI Corporate Agents Regulations 2015, the minimum net worth required for a corporate agent (other than a bank or NBFC regulated by RBI) is:
e: Regulation 7 of the Corporate Agents Regulations 2015 requires applicants (other than those whose principal business is other than insurance distribution, e.g. banks) to have and maintain a minimum net worth of Rs 50 lakh.

topic: IRDA Act 1999 - Duties, Powers and Functions
t: The duties, powers and functions of the IRDAI, including regulating, promoting and ensuring orderly growth of the insurance business, are enumerated in which section of the IRDA Act 1999?
e: Section 14 of the IRDA Act 1999 lists the duties, powers and functions of the Authority, from issuing registration certificates to protecting policyholders' interests and specifying codes of conduct.

t: The National Pension System (NPS) and pension funds are regulated by:
o: PFRDA (Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority)
e: The PFRDA Act 2013 vests regulation of NPS and pension funds in PFRDA; IRDAI regulates insurers' pension/annuity products, SEBI regulates securities and mutual funds, and RBI regulates banks and NBFCs.

topic: IRDAI Surveyors and Loss Assessors Regulations 2015
t: Licensed surveyors and loss assessors in India are categorised into:
o: Grade A, Grade B and Grade C
Class I, Class II and Class III
e: The IRDAI (Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors) Regulations 2015 categorise surveyors as Licentiate, Associate and Fellow based on qualifications, experience and examinations, with membership of IIISLA.

t: The requirement that an insurer must invest its assets only in approved securities and in the manner prescribed by the Authority is contained in:
e: Sections 27, 27A and 27B of the Insurance Act govern investment of assets by life and general insurers, supplemented by IRDAI (Investment) Regulations.
